pool.text: Two towns formed an alliance with common external policy while keeping separate administrations.
Frederick II initiated construction of a new royal palace in Berlin‑Cölln.
Town citizens protested the palace building, known as the Berlin Indignation.
Berlin‑Cölln palace became permanent residence of Brandenburg electors.
Electors and city officially adopted Lutheranism.
Französisches Gymnasium Berlin was founded for Huguenot refugee children.
Berlin hosted the Summer Olympics and built the Olympic stadium.
Monument commemorating Prussia's victories was relocated from in front of the Reichstag.
Soviet blockade of West Berlin prompted the Allied Berlin Airlift.
Tierpark Friedrichsfelde, Berlin’s second zoo, opened.
East Germany erected the Berlin Wall encircling West Berlin.
President Kennedy delivered his "Ich bin ein Berliner" speech.
Four‑Power Agreement guaranteed road and rail access to West Berlin.
The European Film Academy was established in Berlin.
Historic Mitte buildings were occupied and rebuilt by squatters after the Wall fell.
Berlin Wall fell on 9 November, leading to its demolition.
German reunification restored Berlin as the capital of a united Germany.
Allied troops marched in a parade marking the end of occupation.
Construction began on the new Berlin Brandenburg Airport.
Historic Tempelhof Airport closed as part of traffic infrastructure reforms.
